title: Chunking Power
subtitle: Break huge numbers and long sequences into bite-sized brain snacks!

sections.prompt: Can you remember this 10-digit number in 5 seconds: 9812406735?
sections.subtext: It feels almost impossible until you group the digits!

panels.text: Aarav needs to remember his mother's new phone number: 9812406735. The 10 digits look like an impenetrable wall of numbers!
Professor Piko explains: 'Working memory can only hold 3 to 4 items at once. But you can pack multiple digits into a single chunk!'
Instead of 10 separate numbers, group them: [981] - [240] - [6735]. Say it with a musical rhythm: 981... 240... 67-35!
Wow! 3 chunks are just as easy to remember as 3 single digits! My brain loves chunks!
CHUNK-BOT 3000 ONLINE! Let's slice and group big data streams in the simulation!

sections.title: Working Memory & The 3-4 Chunk Rule
sections.summary: 1. Working memory limit: 3–4 items  |  2. Combine adjacent digits into meaningful blocks  |  3. Add rhythm/cadence to lock it in

interactions: Hit Test Chunking to verify rhythm and structure
config.completionCondition: All 3 digit chunks formed with correct grouping

questions.prompt: Why does chunking make long sequences easy to remember?

options.label: It turns 10 individual items into 3 grouped units, fitting our working memory capacity
It makes the numbers smaller in value

hints: Our working memory can comfortably handle 3–4 chunks at once.
